 Fact-check claims before believing them, Onn Hafiz urges Johoreans
 By NELSON BENJAMIN  and  N.S. SRI HAREE 
 Monday, 16 Nov 2026
 | 1:57 PM MYT

 JOHOR BARU: Johoreans have been advised to be careful and to fact-check all information following some online postings, which have made serious allegations and slanderous claims about development and public infrastructure projects here, says the Johor Mentri Besar.
 Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi ( pic ), who flagged those social media accounts, said that many of the postings did not have followers but used the same words and similar narratives, alleging that the projects involved were worth hundreds of millions of ringgit.
 "What is suspicious is that they even named companies with peculiar and dubious names," he said, adding that he had since lodged a police report and filed a complaint with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
 He urged Bangsa Johor to be careful and to verify the facts before believing or spreading such information.
 Onn Hafiz stressed that he was always open to receiving criticism and complaints from Bangsa Johor and assured them that all complaints would be reviewed and acted upon.
 "But we cannot take it lightly if there are parties intentionally using fake accounts to fabricate stories to provoke the public.
 "During this election season, I hope everyone practises politics in a mature and responsible manner," he said, cautioning that everyone could have differences of opinion and offer criticism, but should not allow political differences to be a reason to spread slander and mislead the people.
 Onn Hafiz hoped that the authorities would carry out the necessary investigations, including into the authenticity of the accounts, the content being spread and the possible existence of a coordinated activity.
 "I hope the necessary action can be taken regarding this matter," he said.
 In his post Onn Hafiz also shared at least five of the suspicious postings along with the names of the companies and their allegations.
